title: Nonzero relative differential gives a smooth hypersurface point
statement: Let $p:W\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $s\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal M)$, and let $Z=Z(s)\subseteq W$ be its zero scheme [def-pc-zero-scheme]. Fix $z\in Z$ and a trivialization of $\mathcal M$ near $z$, writing $s=f$ there. Let $df(z)$ denote the image of the universal relative differential of $f$ in $\Omega^1_{W/S,z}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{W,z}}\kappa(z)$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-weil-residue-field]. If $df(z)\ne0$, then $Z\to S$ is smooth at $z$, meaning that it is smooth on some open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$. No flatness assumption on $Z\to S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth, (1), applied after adjoining one equation with an extra nonzero Jacobian row to a standard smooth presentation (Definition 00T6, definition-standard-smooth); smooth charts are Morphisms Tag 01V7, lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth.

proof.text: On the stalks R = O_{S,p(x)}, P = O_{X,x}, and C = O_{Z,z}, use the local equation for the zero scheme to identify ker(P → C) with the principal ideal generated by the germ of a.

A nonzero residue differential is detected by a linear functional on the residue-field tensor of the relative differential stalk. The sheaf universal derivation and the germ compatibility extend this functional to an R-derivation P → κ(x), and then to κ(z), whose value on the germ of a is nonzero. The universal property of Kaehler differentials therefore gives nonvanishing of 1 ⊗ da in κ(z) ⊗[P] Ω[P/R].

The smooth ambient morphism gives formal smoothness and finite free Kähler differentials on the local ring P. The cotangent map from the principal kernel is generated by 1 ⊗ a, and its image is the nonzero vector 1 ⊗ da; hence the map is injective. Mathlib’s local cotangent Jacobian criterion yields formal smoothness of C over R. The Lean proof uses Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_injective_cotangentComplexBaseChange (Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Local); Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing gives freeness of the finite projective differential module. The principal-kernel injectivity argument is proved in the private helper formallySmooth_of_principal_kernel.

The zero ideal is locally principal, so the subscheme morphism composed with p is locally of finite presentation. Its smooth locus is open, contains z by the formal-smooth stalk calculation, and its inclusion gives the required smooth neighbourhood. In Lean, use IsLocallyPrincipal.locallyOfFinitePresentation_subschemeι_comp, Scheme.Hom.smoothLocus_eq_top_iff and Scheme.Hom.preimage_smoothLocus_eq.
